chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Smitty later in Erskine Hawkins's band and Tippin' In
summary: Smitty later played saxophone with Erskine Hawkins and wrote 'Tippin' In'; the interviewer cannot find him in Rust.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: The next time I saw Smitty, which was years later, he was playing saxophone in Erskine Hawkins' band -- Smitty was. And he was a very good saxophone player. I think he's in California now. Because he went to Europe with...
Is his last name Smith?
Yeah. I don't know what his first name is. Not Jimmy Smith...
Well, there doesn't seem to be... He didn't do any recordings.
Well, he recorded with Erskine Hawkins. He was in the band.
He did?

Yeah, he was in Erskine's band for quite a while. The next thing I heard about him, he was in California. He made a trip over to Europe with the same group Howard was with. I think it was the first year you
Holmes (10/9) - 38
went over there.
There doesn't seem to be a Smith.
Well, he wasn't a leader or anything.
No. But he's not listed in Rust.
Well, he wouldn't be listed unless he did something. Unless he was in one of the big-name bands or something. The only name band I'd known him to be in was Erskine Hawkins.
Because the personnel of the sax sections of Erskine Hawkins has William Johnson, Jimmy Mitchell, Paul Bascomb and Haywood Henry.
Yeah, I remember that.
And Julian Dash.
Yes.
But there's no Smith.
Yeah. Well, he was later. 'Tippin' In.' That's the name. I don't know what else he's written. He turned out to be a very good musician.
He's supposed to have written 'Tippin' In'?
That's his number, yeah. Written it and arranged it.
Because I've got Erskine Hawkins' early stuff here, and I don't see that he's recorded it even.
[ETCETERA]
